findings.text: the node record states job 1276081 reported exit 1 in 55 s; sacct records that job Start 20:53:10, End 20:53:20, Elapsed 00:00:10 and ExitCode 1:0, so the exit status is right and the wall is not, and the same 55 s figure is repeated in docs/evidence/archive/plasma-cell-topology-authority-landed.html; correct the figure in both records or drop the wall.

both live lanes ran against an uncommitted worktree: job 1276079 started 20:51:51 and job 1276081 20:53:10, while the test commit 0f150a662 was created at 20:54:17, so after_suite.revision names a revision that post-dates the measurement and after.log's first line reads head 1cfd3fd4c2+repin; the delivered content is corroborated (the commit's diff is the same 22-line change and the negative traceback's line 347 anchor matches the committed file), but committing before the gate would make the revision field checkable from the log alone.

the receipt's spline_authored field is assigned converged, so an assertion on it establishes convergence only; the reviewed test now pins authorship by value, but the field name overstates what it carries for every other consumer of the receipt.

the added tolerance leg compares the published value with the map's value at the seed normalised by the field span, reading 0 when the test passes and 4.547e-13 under the declared mutation against a bound of 5.32e-10, so it cannot fire on the substitution class this node guards and is not a second independent leg; the discrimination is the bit-for-bit comparison at line 346.

item_verdicts.diff: Substantially sound. The 22-line diff replaces the false inequality with a construction check (the census slot offset from the map value at the seed by 2^-40 = 9.094947017729282e-13, byte-distinct, and 4.547473508864641e-13 once normalised by the field span, about 1170 times inside the receipt's dimensionless tolerance 5.323563998270512e-10), keeps the bit-for-bit equality against the receipt spline_value, adds the published-versus-map tolerance leg normalised as the receipt normalises normalized_value_change (field_scale at flux_surface_connectivity.py:1217 is the field span), and keeps every named assertion. The baseline lane shows the removed assertion was false, not merely weak: published, spline_value and the census literal are all the binary64 ae47e17a14aed73f at base.
item_verdicts.done_when: Met in the deliverable, with two defects in the landed record. The construction, the kept assertions, the one-mechanism comments, one all_debug job per lane, the baseline failure of exactly that test, the after pass, the declared mutation verbatim as the red log's first line and the ruff checks are all present and corroborated. The record's claim that the negative job reported exit 1 in 55 s is not: sacct records that job at 10 s elapsed, and both the plan and the anchor repeat the figure.
item_verdicts.goal: Met. The re-pinned test measures authorship of the published value directly: the published bytes must equal the receipt spline_value bit for bit, with the census slot made byte-distinct from the map's own value at the seed, replacing an inequality against the raw census bytes that measured nothing.
item_verdicts.manifest: Complete and checkable with two wording blemishes: status complete, two commits, three changed paths, both suite JSONs with exit statuses matching the logs, and the negative log named alone; the record omits the four wait keys, which nothing requires once terminal, and its artifacts prose carries a garbled fragment where the baseline wall belongs.
item_verdicts.write_paths: Respected. The three changed paths are exactly the declared test file, the plan and the landed anchor; the plan diff is three inserted record paragraphs and no version, followup or status line; the reports fence holds every log and scratch script.

justifications.durability: The change is committed (test at 0f150a662, record at d2d14c063) and strictly strengthens the pin, and the negative script carries its own positive control (exit 77 if the mutation did not fail), so the red log is non-vacuous. What it does not do: the receipt's spline_authored key aliases converged, so the assertion on it re-states convergence rather than authorship; and the added tolerance leg reads 0 in the passing case and 4.547e-13 under the guarded mutation against a 5.32e-10 bound, so it cannot discriminate that mutation and the pin rests on the bit-for-bit leg alone.
justifications.evidence: Three lanes with logs on disk and jobs verified against sacct: 1276077 FAILED 1:0 in 58 s, 1276079 COMPLETED 0:0 in 57 s, 1276081 FAILED 1:0 in 10 s, matching the baseline 1 failed/14 passed and the after 15 passed, with the negative traceback naming the authorship assertion itself at the bit-for-bit leg. Two defects hold the score down: the record's negative-job wall of 55 s is contradicted by sacct's 10 s, and both live lanes ran while the re-pin was uncommitted (jobs start 20:51:51 and 20:53:10; the test commit is 20:54:17), so after_suite.revision names a commit that post-dates the measurement while the log's own header reads head 1cfd3fd4c2+repin; the negative traceback's line anchors match the committed file, so the content agrees, but after_suite.revision cannot be checked from the log alone.
justifications.fit: The re-pin strengthens an existing regression test rather than reimplementing the production path, records on the plan and the landed anchor in the project's convention, and states that merged-head verification of the section belongs to the coordinator's separately dispatched test node; the section, driving followup and plan status are unchanged.
justifications.goal_fidelity: The deliverable does what the goal names, in the only form that can: with the exact quadratic reproducing a paraboloid value bit for bit, a difference against the census bytes measured nothing, so authorship is pinned by equality with the receipt spline_value and by the published value matching the map's own value at the seed. It also converts a silently false assertion into a true one, which the baseline lane demonstrates at line 344.
justifications.scope_discipline: Exactly the declared paths: the test file, the plan, the landed anchor, with every log and scratch script under the reports fence. The plan record is appended only, and nothing under another node's fence appears anywhere in the diff.
